observations.summary: The GUI distinguishes tab-local filtering from object-first, run-aware Orchestrator search that routes results to canonical objects.
Concern surfaces preserve evidence, source references, lineage, remediation, recovery, and review or graph-patch relationships; merge, split, and supersede are guided structural flows.
Projection-backed UI exposes freshness and health terminology, five freshness states, update/source/reason fields, and mutation gating tied to currentness and trust.

Only Progress remains widget-hosted in native Orchestrator; tier-era widgets and aliases are compatibility vocabulary, active writes use widget_layout, and retired keys are read-only migration backups.
Blocked notices expose sequence, approval scope, report, recovery, action, and escalation data; blocked_sequence is the approval identity and ordered allowed_action_ids drive graph HITL actions.
Bulk and recovery actions are gated through confirmation strength, runtime-defined allowed actions, freshness, account capability, runtime capability, and safe exact-action batch semantics.
Canonical terms, help, and contextual help have distinct owners; notifications preserve severity, source, owner route, and a strict distinction between resolution and dismissal or acknowledgment.
Routes target named shell destinations, selectors refine the landing, route arguments override remembered defaults, and Contracts_V0 owns the payload and object_kind model.

project_summary is overwritten by projector updates, while project_attention_item retains active and presentation-state distinctions plus a stable source_object_ref when durable history lives elsewhere.

Provider-account intent is separated from policy and operational identity; user-facing runtime identity must include requested/effective account truth, actor role, execution role, target context, switch history, and trust state.
The authoritative GUI direction is a Rust and Slint IDE shell with redb, seglog, Tantivy, and deterministic renderer precedence from explicit override through software fallback.

The first implementation includes native and Slint/WASM targets; browser OS authority is daemon-mediated, capability receipts are authoritative, and the capability matrix assigns exact native and web states.
Production visuals use bundled SVG icon_ids without emoji or remote icon assets, while development and automation controls are excluded from production unless explicitly authorized and audited.

PMConcept is source-lineage only; production wiring comes from the wiring matrix, command catalog, and owner documents, and the Planning Wizard uses dynamic PlanningRun state rather than a fixed phase rail.
Approve And Build is the sole ordinary approval-to-compile launch authority; testing projections, accessibility behavior, and fixture redaction are all explicit implementation-readiness obligations.
Both addenda explicitly exclude WorkNodes, executable queues, implementation/runtime creation, generated governance artifacts, and governance sealing.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical concern record shape is absent
candidate_findings.summary: The assigned core declares a concern-record family, references a canonical schema, and later presents a Recommended minimum concern record shape heading, but supplies no exact field names, types, requiredness, identifiers, cardinalities, or serialized shape.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders must invent the persisted and projected concern schema and decide which routing, remediation, graph, recovery, review, patch, and lineage data are mandatory.

candidate_findings.title: Concern merge, split, and supersede lack executable action contracts
candidate_findings.summary: The intended lineage outcomes and guided-flow requirement are stated, but the assigned core does not define command identities, actor authority, preconditions, conflict or CAS behavior, receipt effects, atomicity, rollback, or error recovery for these structural mutations.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Independent implementations can mutate lineage differently, permit different actors, or leave partially updated concern and history records after failure.

candidate_findings.title: Projection health and stale-action behavior are nondeterministic
candidate_findings.summary: The text names projection_health but defines only freshness_state values. For stale or degraded projections it permits multiple alternatives—narrow, disable, or revalidate—and current projections merely may allow read/write interaction. The dedicated freshness-versus-health heading has no body.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders must invent projection_health values, freshness/health combinations, transition rules, and the exact action-gate outcome for each mutation.

candidate_findings.title: Widget layout scope retains unresolved alternatives
candidate_findings.summary: The dashboard may remain app-global, orchestrator:progress may be project-scoped or use app-default plus project override, and usage chooses between app-wide and project-scoped modes, despite the same core claiming deterministic defaults and no open questions.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders can choose incompatible storage keys, inheritance rules, and cross-project behavior for the same layouts.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked approval identity and escalation fields lack exact semantics
candidate_findings.summary: blocked_sequence, approval_scope_key, escalation_level, startup_recovered, action_available, and ordered allowed_action_ids are required, but their types, uniqueness scope, monotonicity, episode rollover, invalidation, and mapping to legacy request_id or hitl_request_id are not defined in the assigned core.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders must decide how approvals are correlated and invalidated, creating risk that stale or cross-episode actions target the wrong blocked state.

candidate_findings.title: Confirmation and batch-mutation policy lacks deterministic thresholds
candidate_findings.summary: The text does not define light or strong confirmation behavior, an exact escalation matrix, or the schema and evaluation order for the listed gates. It also lists both allowed_action_ids and allowed_action_ids[] without defining whether they are aliases or distinct preconditions, and leaves safe batch semantics to runtime exposure without a contract shape.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Destructive and topology-changing actions can receive different confirmation strength, authority checks, and batch behavior across surfaces.

candidate_findings.title: Project summary projection has no local schema
candidate_findings.summary: The Project summary projection heading is empty. The following text establishes overwrite behavior and attention-item lineage but does not define project_summary fields, identity, timestamps, trust state, update atomicity, unavailable behavior, or projector failure handling.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders must invent the summary payload and decide how incomplete, stale, or failed projector updates appear in the GUI.

candidate_findings.title: Rationale enforcement and blocked-owner eight-kind taxonomy are empty
candidate_findings.summary: The assigned core contains headings for freshness versus health, dismissed-versus-resolved rationale enforcement, an eight-kind blocked-owner taxonomy and escalation surfaces, and a recommended concern shape, but provides no body for those sections.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders cannot know the eight kinds, owner mapping, escalation ladder, rationale requirements, validation failures, or required display behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Operational and requested-account identity blocks lack an exact GUI data contract
candidate_findings.summary: The required identity concepts are enumerated, but the assigned core does not define field types, required versus conditional presence, unknown or unavailable values, redaction rules, concrete-account display safety, switch-history ordering, or how trust state gates identity claims.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Different surfaces can expose inconsistent or overly revealing identity data while still claiming to satisfy the conceptual field list.

candidate_findings.title: Toolchain recertification has no evidence or failure contract
candidate_findings.summary: Production work must re-check official Rust and Slint releases, but the assigned core does not define the checker, authority, timestamp freshness, recorded receipt, acceptable version relationship, or disposition when pinned and current versions differ.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: A builder can claim certification using different sources or evidence and can independently decide whether a version delta blocks implementation.

candidate_findings.title: Approved web toolchain, bootstrap, and local-service boundaries are undefined
candidate_findings.summary: The web contract permits an approved equivalent toolchain, minimal bootstrap glue, and approved local services without naming the approval authority, allowlist, change process, or measurable boundary for minimal JavaScript.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders can introduce materially different toolchains, bootstrap behavior, and service connections while treating them as approved equivalents.

candidate_findings.title: Trusted-daemon security requirements lack implementable protocol semantics
candidate_findings.summary: Authentication or pairing, origin and CSRF protection, capability probes, permission requests, receipts, redaction, and degraded behavior are mandatory, but the assigned core does not define trust bootstrap, session/token lifecycle, origin rules, revocation, request/response schemas, permission scope, receipt schema, replay protection, or denial and transport-failure behavior.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: The OS-capability security boundary can be implemented with incompatible or insufficient authority and audit guarantees.

candidate_findings.title: Web capability states lack probe-to-state transition rules
candidate_findings.summary: The exact state vocabulary and per-family matrix are present, but the assigned core does not specify initial state, probe timing, daemon disconnect transitions, permission-denial transitions, recovery, stale receipt behavior, or which state wins when direct and daemon-mediated alternatives coexist.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Capability indicators and enabled controls can diverge under startup, disconnect, denial, or narrowed-daemon conditions.

candidate_findings.title: Production authorization for dev and automation controls is underspecified
candidate_findings.summary: Production builds may expose dev/test, MCP, live-preview, fixture, or browser-automation controls when an explicit production configuration authorizes them, but the configuration owner, schema, signing or trust source, per-capability scope, revocation, visibility, and required audit receipt are not defined.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Sensitive testing or automation controls can be enabled through incompatible configuration paths with inconsistent user disclosure and auditability.

candidate_findings.title: Approve And Build lacks atomicity and replay behavior
candidate_findings.summary: The command must validate displayed CAS inputs, write a receipt, publish an event, synchronously create or bind exactly one run, and navigate, but the assigned core does not define transaction boundaries, idempotency key, CAS-mismatch response, retry or replay semantics, partial-failure compensation, or behavior when navigation fails after durable launch.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: A retry after partial failure can duplicate events or runs, lose the approval receipt, or show a state inconsistent with the durable PlanCompileRun despite the exactly-one requirement.

candidate_findings.title: Testing settings and active-session controls lack exact state semantics
candidate_findings.summary: Global and project rows, inherited/effective state, Auto/On/Off, show_when_possible, and active-session actions are required, but precedence, capability-unavailable behavior, state transitions, command identities, disabled reasons, failure states, and evidence or redaction receipt effects are not defined.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders must invent how settings resolve and when Open, Watch, detach, background, evidence inspection, and redaction inspection are available.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility obligations lack pass/fail evidence criteria
candidate_findings.summary: Required accessible names, roles, keyboard parity, focus, disclosure semantics, and disabled-reason association are listed, but wiring evidence is not defined and there is no required automated or manual test matrix, platform coverage, acceptance receipt, or mapping for Slint equivalents to DOM-specific aria-describedby.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Builders can provide different evidence and semantic mappings while claiming implementation readiness.

candidate_findings.title: Fixture redaction and evidence safety lack exact schemas and validation
candidate_findings.summary: The forbidden data classes and required redacted projections are explicit, but the assigned core does not define the redaction-manifest schema, path and URL detection rules, credential-summary allowlist, secret scanning, false-positive disposition, evidence linkage, or acceptance test proving prohibited values are absent.
candidate_findings.consequential_builder_discretion: Sensitive local paths, account details, or misleading fixture evidence can pass under inconsistent redaction implementations.

explicit_non_gaps.summary: Search in this tab and Search Orchestrator have explicitly different scope and landing behavior.
Concern lineage preserves split and supersession history, and duplicate merges retain one identity with redirects rather than overwriting records.
Dismissal or acknowledgment cannot make an active blocker appear resolved; resolution requires the underlying condition to change.
Route overrides take precedence over remembered state, and route-payload ownership is assigned to Contracts_V0.
Operational identity is explicitly distinct from provider-account identity and must appear beside it on side-effect surfaces.
Native renderer precedence, environment-override priority, fallbacks, and required startup diagnostics are explicit.
Browser-only WASM cannot infer OS authority from localhost reachability, and the exact capability-state vocabulary plus per-family native/web disposition are present.
Production visual assets are local SVGs with stable icon_ids; emoji, remote icon imports, and icon-only state communication are explicitly forbidden.
Native and web product-UI technology exclusions are explicit: native is Rust and Slint, and web is Slint/WASM canvas rather than React, Tauri, or DOM product UI.
PMConcept is explicitly noncanonical source-lineage, and its inline handlers, local state, visual styling, demo data, and fixed mock content are not production wiring authority.
Approve And Build is explicitly the sole ordinary final launch authority, and alternative START, BUILD, or Approve & Continue controls cannot create a second launch from the same inputs.
Local paths, localhost URLs, demo databases, sample secrets, raw account details, and misleading terminal or browser evidence are explicitly prohibited as production acceptance proof.
The addenda explicitly do not create implementation work, runtime dispatch, generated governance artifacts, or governance seals.
DAE tool-event history is explicitly barred from authoritative replay until richer payloads and a reconciled outcome taxonomy exist.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: ### Concern record family definition

Global search labels distinguish `Search in this tab` from `Search Orchestrator`: the former is local tab filtering, while the latter is object-first, cross-tab, and route-aware so concern, evidence, history, ledger, and graph results land on the canonical object route rather than a page-local text match.

The active split names `Orchestrator search` as object-first, run-aware, cross-tab routing and `tab-local search` as local `/filtering` within the active tab or `/view`.

- Concern surfaces map `Progress`, `Plan Compile`, `Seams`, `Node Graph`, `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger` views onto concern-linked `/evidence`, `/package` rollups, exact source references, `/split/supersession`, and acknowledgment `/dismissal` rationale instead of flattening concern history into one summary row.
- Concern record surfaces expose a canonical record schema with `/routing`, `/blocked/remediation`, `/corroboration/graph`, `/recovery`, and relationship links to reviews and graph patches; structural actions use `/split/supersession` instead of local free-text history.
- Concern lineage transitions use `merge`, `split`, and `superseded`; when one concern is reframed into several precise concerns, the original resolves with `resolution_kind = split` and retained lineage refs rather than being overwritten.
- Concern updates append new `/evidence` and can raise `/attention`; two duplicate concerns merge into one retained id and `/redirect` the `merged-away` ids, while an older framing replaced by a `/newer` concern is `resolved` with `resolution_kind = superseded`.
- Object-specific context menus show only operational actions valid for the current object state and use canonical labels from runtime semantics; mutation actions never appear because a generic shell menu has a matching verb.
- Structural concern actions such as `merge`, `split`, and `supersede` use guided flows instead of one-click menus because they change `/history/ledger` interpretation and lineage, not only presentation state.

Projection-backed surfaces display `projection_freshness` and `projection_health` as the runtime trust grammar. Preview/browser `/UI` keeps `trust_tier` under `/browser`; runtime `/degraded` copy never reuses `trust_tier` as degraded trust. Artifact provenance `/trust` disclosure derives from persisted receipts and canonical refs, so reports remain inspectable after the live worktree or provider session is gone. `projection-backed` panels expose `trust state` and `last updated` as first-class UI fields.

Shared attention labels include `Waiting on user approval`, `Seam integration blocked`, `Graph patch required`, `Recovery in progress`, `Provider/account pressure`, and `Projection trust degraded`; each label carries owner route, projection state, and `/account` or provider context when relevant instead of acting as free-text status.

Projection-backed surfaces use `freshness_state` values `current`, `refreshing`, `stale`, `degraded`, and `unavailable`; `/current` projections may allow normal read/write interaction, while `stale` or `/degraded` surfaces narrow mutation-bearing actions, disable them, or require direct canonical/current revalidation before execution.

Visible projection trust grammar includes `last_updated_at`, `data_source_kind`, `degraded_reason`, and `action_gate_reason` so operators can see whether a blocked or disabled action comes from freshness, source quality, or an authoritative runtime gate.

- `Plans/Widget_System.md` (`/Widget_System.md`) tier-centric `Orch/Tiers` and `/Tiers` entries, `widget.agent_terminal`, `widget.completed_prose`, `widget.tier_tree`, older `TierChanged` / `IterationStart` pushes, and `/task/subtask`-oriented `widget.current_task` remain compatibility vocabulary; only `Progress` is widget-hosted in the current Orchestrator model.
- Legacy `GUI` inventory entries such as `/current-task`, `7.7 Tiers`, tier-oriented Settings, `Orchestrator tabs`, `wizard_attention_required`, `resume_url`, and phase-task-subtask progress bars stay searchable compatibility copy, but primary navigation moves to native graph/package/lane/seam surfaces rather than treating `Tiers` as canonical.
- Legacy Progress widget catalog fields such as `widget.current_task`, `widget.progress_bars`, `widget.cta_stack`, `widget.agent_terminal`, and `widget.completed_prose` plus `PuppetMasterEvent`, `PuppetMasterEvent::UserInteractionRequired`, `UserInteractionRequired`, `tier_id`, `/tasks`, `/task/subtask`, and `/objective/elapsed` are compatibility inputs only; native Orchestrator views own live progress display.
- `Plans/Widget_System.md` / `/Widget_System.md` migrates `dashboard_layout:v1` to `widget_layout:v1:dashboard`; `widget_layout` is the active layout family while `dashboard_layout` and `dashboard_layout:v1` remain backup/migration names.
- `Widget_System` / `Widget_System.md` keeps `/Tiers`, `Orch/Tiers`, `Orch/Evidence`, `Orch/History`, `Orch/Ledger`, `/Evidence`, `/History`, and `/Ledger` as legacy widget-composed catalog aliases only; only `Progress` remains widget-composed in native Orchestrator.
- Widget persistence scope is explicit: `dashboard` layout may stay app-global, `orchestrator:progress` is project-scoped or app-default plus project override, and `usage` declares app-wide versus project-scoped mode rather than silently reusing one layout.
- `Orchestrator_Page` / `Orchestrator_Page.md` Progress widgets that still center active-tier or tier-targeted terminal semantics are legacy inputs; `widget.agent_terminal`, `widget.completed_prose`, `widget.current_task`, `widget.progress_bars`, `/task/subtask`, and `/objective/platform/model` resolve through native Progress and runtime views.
- The widget layout migration has one explicit persistence-rule: active layout state writes through `widget_layout`, while retired layout keys are read-only migration backups.

Blocked-notice consumers keep `## Unified Thread Blocked-State Lifecycle`, `### Multi-episode display`, and `### 7.3 Shared route and open behavior` as owner-anchor / owner-heading carry-through, but `gap-002`, `exact_items`, `stale-survivor`, and `GUI` cleanup must expose `blocked_sequence`, `approval_scope_key`, `report_ref`, `startup_recovered`, `action_available`, and `escalation_level` instead of leaving those fields in a skeletal blocked-notice flow.

`Plans/Run_Graph_View.md` (`/Run_Graph_View.md`) `cmd.graph.approve_hitl` / `cmd.graph.deny_hitl` actions use `blocked_sequence` and ordered `allowed_action_ids[]`; legacy `hitl_request_id` is compatibility display metadata, not a second `HITL` approval identity.

`Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md` (`/UI_Command_Catalog.md`) graph HITL command examples with `{ request_id, node_id, rationale }` and `{ request_id, node_id, rationale, resolution? }` map to the same runtime approval identity; `request_id` and `node_id` are routing/lineage args, not a replacement for `blocked_sequence`.

- Bulk live actions such as `/remove`, `/recovery`, archive/prune, or worktree cleanup choose `light`, `strong`, or `hard_gate` confirmation based on blocked/recovery lineage and target preview; destructive `remove` defaults to `strong`, and blocked-lineage recovery can escalate to `hard_gate`.
- A `hard_gate` confirmation must show runtime-defined allowed actions, why the gate exists, the exact consequence of each allowed action, and no hidden alternative path.
- Runtime mutation and `/recovery` surfaces require `/schema/gate` preconditions for `allowed_action_ids`, `allowed_action_ids[]`, freshness `/trust`, account capability, and `/runtime` capability before the GUI exposes mutation controls.
- Bulk actions default to navigation, triage, and low-risk state updates; live execution mutations stay narrow unless the runtime exposes an explicit safe batch semantic for that exact action.
- Stale visibility is not action authority: when projection trust drops, `/recovery` controls and `allowed_action_ids[]` may become invalid, and destructive or topology-changing actions require stronger gating rather than ordinary undo.
- `Plans/Tools.md` (`/Tools.md`) DAE tool-event reconstruction requires richer event payloads and reconciled outcome taxonomy before GUI surfaces can replay DAE tool-event history as authoritative runtime state.

- The canonical term system owns stable object `/state/action` names from docs and `/runtime/contracts`; the help entry system owns explainer pages or `/cards`; the contextual help system owns inline tooltips, badges, hover copy, and small "what is this?" affordances.

Notification and attention copy use the shared state/action label set: `alert-level`, `event-family`, backbone event, `/action`, and condition-aging taxonomy terms are routed through `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md`, `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` (`/Orchestrator_Page.md`), and `Plans/Glossary.md` (`/Glossary.md`) rather than ad hoc local labels.

Alert-state semantics remain explicit across Dashboard and attention-surface copy for `attention_required` and `blocked` states: `resolved` means the underlying condition changed; `dismissed` or `/acknowledged` only hides or confirms presentation while the condition may still exist, and active blockers must never appear unblocked through dismissal alone.

Local attention surfaces normalize through the shared notification model: Dashboard `Action Required`, thread badges, run-graph `/node` badges, warnings `/toasts/banners`, tray `/system` notifications, rate-limit banners, and blocked versus attention-required copy all preserve severity, source, and owner route instead of inventing local alert state.

Tab badges stay sparse and purposeful: the `Progress` badge represents meaningful `/action-required` count, while other tabs prefer targeted counts or simple dot-badges rather than noisy unread-like counters.

Route payloads may target `source_control`, `github_actions`, `docker_manager`, or `document_pane`; panel-local subviews and `/selectors` refine the landing inside that destination, and remembered state supplies defaults only when the route does not override them.

Object-first deep-link recipes normalize `/message`, scheduler `/blocking/safe-point/remediation/attempt`, and `/package/lane/worktree/concern/promotion/graph` lineage through one route shape; `Plans/assistant-chat-design.md`, `Plans/Run_Graph_View.md`, `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md`, and `Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md` consume the same object-first routing instead of inventing an SCM-local navigation identity.

`Contracts_V0` / `Contracts_V0.md` owns the canonical route payload and target model, including the `object_kind` enum; `Glossary.md` carries the user-facing `object_kind` vocabulary so help and downstream copy do not drift.

> **Compliance:** This document follows `Plans/DRY_Rules.md` and references SSOT contracts in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`. Naming: “Puppet Master” only. No open questions; deterministic defaults per `Plans/Decision_Policy.md`.

**Date:** 2026-02-22
**Status:** Authoritative specification for AI agent implementation
**Tech Stack:** Rust stable 1.96.1 + Slint 1.17.1 (.slint markup compiled via slint_build)
**Renderer:** Native desktop uses Slint Winit with Skia compiled in and selected by default; fallback is Winit + FemtoVG-wgpu, then Winit software renderer only as an emergency path.

This document is the authoritative GUI specification for the Puppet Master desktop application, replacing the retired Rust/Iced-lineage GUI with a Slint 1.17.1 implementation on Rust stable 1.96.1. The design follows an IDE-shell layout (Activity Bar + Primary Content + Side Panel + Bottom Panel) with three user-facing theme families (Retro Dark, Retro Light, Basic Modern) backed by deterministic built-in palette variants plus user-created custom themes, detachable panels, and a rearrangeable dashboard.

The current GUI uses a two-row header with 16 flat navigation buttons above a single full-width content area. This wastes screen real estate and forces constant page-switching. The new layout follows a three-column IDE shell inspired by VS Code / JetBrains, dressed in the existing retro-futuristic aesthetic.

Key changes from the retired Rust/Iced-lineage GUI:
- **Layout:** Single-page-at-a-time replaced with persistent IDE shell (Activity Bar, Primary Content, Side Panel, Bottom Panel)
- **Navigation:** 16 flat buttons replaced with 5-group Activity Bar + Command Palette
- **Settings restructure:** Old `Settings` becomes `App Settings`; old `Config` becomes `Settings`; Login and Doctor merge into unified Settings
- **New views:** Usage page, File Manager panel, editor surface, Chat panel, Agent Activity pane, Artifacts, Source Control, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, and Run & Debug side-panel surfaces
- **Bottom runtime zone:** Terminal, Problems, Output, Ports, and the classical **Debugger** / **DAP Debugger** live here; normal browsing and HTML preview remain editor-tab or detached-window browser surfaces rather than bottom-panel tabs
- Coarse surface vocabulary treats primary-content pages `/views`, side-panel destinations, bottom-panel surfaces, and Orchestrator tabs as shell categories, not interchangeable route identities.
- **Themes:** Three theme families with full extensibility and deterministic built-in variants
- **Real-time:** Event-driven updates via Rust channels and `invoke_from_event_loop`, not polling
- **Panels:** Chat and File Manager are detachable; shell state remains identity-safe when re-docked
- **Project bar:** Instant project switching from title bar with full state preservation and reload
- **Language detection:** Auto-detect project languages, display badges, and suggest LSP/tool presets
- **Sound effects:** Optional audio feedback for key events via `rodio`
- **Catalog and sync:** Community content catalog with install/update/remove flows and config export/import bundles
- **SSH remote editing:** Edit files on remote hosts via SSH/SFTP with connection management and offline resilience
- **Debug workflows:** Assistant Debug Mode is a first-class chat workflow overlay; the classical DAP surface remains a separate debugger surface

| Language | Rust stable 1.96.1 | All logic, state management, and Slint bridge code; verified current stable on 2026-07-02 |
| UI Framework | Slint 1.17.1 | `.slint` markup files compiled via `slint_build` in `build.rs`; selected by owner decision on 2026-07-07 |
| Default Renderer | Winit + Skia | Skia is compiled in for Windows, Linux, and macOS native desktop builds and is the default renderer |
| Fallback Renderer | Winit + FemtoVG-wgpu | Used when Skia is unavailable after explicit override and persisted-preference resolution |
| Emergency Renderer | Winit software renderer | Last resort for headless, CI, unsupported GPU, or emergency recovery environments |
| Persistence (layout) | redb | Durable KV store for layout state, preferences, editor state |
| Persistence (events) | seglog | Canonical event ledger for usage, chat, orchestrator events |
| Search | Tantivy | Full-text search index over seglog projections |

Toolchain currentness is a certification input, not PMConcept evidence. Runtime implementation or production build packets must re-check the official Rust stable channel and Slint current stable release before code work starts; stale PMConcept terminal transcripts, demo version strings, and old audit references are concept/source-lineage fixtures only.

Native desktop targets Windows, Linux, and macOS through the Slint Winit backend. The compiled renderer availability order is Winit + Skia, Winit + FemtoVG-wgpu, then Winit software renderer. Runtime selection resolves in this order: `SLINT_BACKEND` explicit override, persisted renderer preference, compiled Skia default, FemtoVG-wgpu fallback, and software emergency fallback. `SLINT_BACKEND` remains valid for debugging, CI, and operator override, but persisted preferences must not silently override an explicit environment override. Startup diagnostics record the requested backend, effective backend, fallback reason, platform, GPU/driver summary when available, and whether the fallback was operator-selected or automatic.

The first GUI implementation includes both the native desktop target and a Slint Rust WASM web GUI. The web GUI is a Slint/WASM canvas client compiled as a Rust `cdylib` with `wasm-bindgen`, `wasm-pack`, or an approved equivalent toolchain and loaded by a minimal HTML/canvas bootstrap. The web target does not use React, Tauri, or DOM-rendered product UI. Browser JavaScript is limited to generated or minimal bootstrap glue needed to load the WASM canvas client, route static assets, attach the canvas, and connect to approved local services.

Browser-only WASM is not allowed to pretend it owns OS capabilities. It must not claim direct ownership of PTY, project filesystem mutation or watching, process/container execution, CEF-class browser embedding, system tray, native windows, native child windows, or raw native OS drag/drop. When a capability is unavailable in the browser sandbox, the UI shows the capability state, degraded reason, and the approved native or daemon-mediated route.

### 2.4 Trusted Local Daemon Contract

The web GUI may use OS-owned capabilities only through a trusted local Puppet Master daemon. The daemon boundary requires authenticated local origin or pairing, origin and CSRF protection, capability probing before feature enablement, explicit permission requests for sensitive operations, receipt/audit events for granted or denied actions, redaction before display or persistence, degraded reasons when the daemon is absent or narrowed, and deterministic agent-test hooks for fixture mode and browser automation. The web GUI consumes daemon capability receipts; it does not infer authority from localhost reachability alone.

Web capability state values are exactly `native_full`, `web_supported_direct`, `web_supported_via_trusted_local_daemon`, `web_simulated_or_degraded`, and `web_disabled`.

| Capability family | Native desktop state | Web state | Required web alternative |
|-------------------|----------------------|-----------|--------------------------|
| Terminal/PTY | `native_full` | `web_supported_via_trusted_local_daemon` | Daemon-owned PTY session stream, permission receipt, redacted transcript/evidence |
| Git, process, and container operations | `native_full` | `web_supported_via_trusted_local_daemon` | Daemon-owned command execution, capability probe, audit receipt, disabled/degraded reason |
| Project filesystem watching and mutation | `native_full` | `web_supported_via_trusted_local_daemon` | Project-root grant, watch proxy, FileSafe/permission receipt, redacted path display |
| Browser automation | `native_full` | `web_supported_via_trusted_local_daemon` | Daemon-owned automation session with screenshots, state capture, console/network receipt |
| CEF embedding / native child browser host | `native_full` | `web_disabled` | Evidence stream, in-canvas browser status panels, or browser popup clients when permitted |
| System tray and OS notifications/tray menu | `native_full` | `web_disabled` | Status page, in-canvas notification center, browser notification permission where supported |
| Native detached Slint windows and redock | `native_full` | `web_simulated_or_degraded` | In-canvas panels, browser popup clients, persisted layout state without OS window authority |
| Raw native OS drag/drop paths | `native_full` | `web_supported_via_trusted_local_daemon` | File drops, project-root grants, browser File API metadata, daemon-mediated path binding |

Production GUI surfaces use bundled local SVG assets referenced by stable `icon_id`. The production UI must not use emoji, emoji-like pictographs, Dingbat-style pseudo-icons, or Unicode pictographs as controls, badges, status indicators, or decorative substitutes for icons. Concept glyphs from PMConcept or other source-lineage artifacts map only to approved `icon_id` entries before promotion.

The local SVG manifest includes `icon_id`, file path, semantic label, theme behavior, size slots, accessible label, fallback text, and any state-variant mapping. Icons are never the sole carrier of state: every icon-only control has an accessible label, tooltip or equivalent label projection, keyboard/focus behavior, and nearby or programmatic state text. Network/CDN icon fonts or remote SVG/icon imports are forbidden for production GUI source.

### 2.7 GUI Web Dev/Test Workflow

The web GUI development workflow uses a local trusted daemon plus a static web route, fixture mode, browser automation smoke tests, screenshots/state capture, deterministic state hooks, and fast rebuild/reload loops. Development preview controls may expose reload, fixture-mode selection, screenshot/state capture, and daemon capability inspection only in configured development or automated-test builds. Production builds must not enable dev/test, MCP, live-preview, fixture, or browser automation controls unless an explicit production configuration authorizes that capability and records the permission/audit surface.

Native product UI does not use React, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Tauri, or DOM-rendered controls. The native desktop GUI is Rust + Slint `.slint` markup. The web GUI uses Rust Slint compiled to WASM canvas plus minimal bootstrap glue only; it is not a React/Tauri/web-DOM product UI.
